questions.q: Which of these sounds most like you?

options.text: You'd rather take the extra time to do something carefully and get it right than move fast on a hunch.
You tend to spot the angle everyone else missed and plan around it before it turns into a problem.
You go after what you actually want, instead of adjusting to others' rules.
You trust what feels true to you over advice about what you're supposed to want.
You feel most like yourself as part of something bigger — a group, a cause, a belief.

questions.q: At your best, you're the kind of person who...

options.text: Makes sure the person with the least is still looked after.
Uses expertise to bring things closer to perfection.
Gets things done without waiting to be told or helped.
Says the true thing in the room that no one else will.
Stays steady while everyone else spins.

questions.q: Where does a person's responsibility really lie?

options.text: With the people around them — we're all carrying each other.
With themselves first; no one else carries your weight for long.
With getting things right, even when that's slower and harder.
With the role they actually have, not the one they wish they had.
With being honest about what they feel, and acting on it.

questions.q: Laws and traditions are best understood as...

options.text: Promises we keep so the weak aren't left at the mercy of the strong.
Works in progress — to be scrutinized and debated.
Systems of control; worth following when they're convenient to you.
Things that lasted because they quietly work, even when they're unpleasant.
A constraint on your freedom, to be ignored if that's how you feel.

questions.q: When you picture doing right by people, who's actually in front of you?

options.text: Yourself first — take real charge of your own life, so you're a burden to no one and can answer for what you do.
The handful who are truly yours — the people you love come before any cause.
People in abstract — the public, the patients, the citizens, the employees.
The community you belong to — the living whole that holds you up and that you help hold up.
Humanity - every person individually deserves your efforts.

questions.q: A close friend repeats something you'd told them in confidence. When you find out, you...

options.text: Tell them right away how much it stung — they should hear it from you while it's still raw.
Say plainly that it crossed a line; trust has rules, and you'd want to be held to them too.
Hold off reacting until you understand why they did it — there may be more to it than it looks.
Say little, but quietly adjust what you trust them with from here on.
Let it settle, and weigh it against everything they've been to you over the years.

questions.q: How should wealth be distributed in society?

options.text: It should be distributed equally. No one should go hungry, even if that means no one gets to be rich.
Resources should be given to those who can become more productive, and create more wealth for everyone later.
People should rise and fall on their own merits.
Just go help whoever needs it, now. Stop overthinking it.
It's good to distribute some wealth, but too much can cause social disruption. We must keep a careful balance.

questions.q: When you look back on a good year, what made it worth it?

options.text: That you had multiple new experiences, rather than live a boring life.
That you got through it on your own and came out on top of everyone else.
That you reached a concrete milestone you'd set for yourself.
That you didn't go through it alone, and didn't let others either.
That you discovered something new about yourself and grew into a better you.

questions.q: What do people most often get wrong about you?

options.text: They interpret your self-reliance as coldness. You just don't expect to be rescued.
They think you're naive for caring so much about others.
They mistake your responsibility and focus for being boring.
They call you impulsive when you're just living life.
They think you're self-absorbed when you're actually just peaceful.
Feeling. Excitement, love, passion, fun, laughs.
Improving things. To get a better education, to do a better at my job, to learn something new.
Creating a better world, one with more peace and less suffering.
Getting power, to get the things I want and protect those I care about from harm.
Being in harmony, with myself and the world around me. To be well and at peace.
